newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hostages at Japan ambassador's home in Lima.
newsitem.headline: Hostages at Japan ambassador's home in Lima.

text.p: Here is a list of hostages taken by a guerrilla group at the Lima residence of the Japanese ambassador to Peru.
Peru's Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela, Agriculture Minister Rodolfo Munante Sanguineti and speaker of parliament were being held, according to Japan's Kyodo news agency.
Officials in Lima said Peru's Supreme Court President Moises Pantoja and at least three Peruvian legislators were also there.
Japan's Foreign Ministry aid arm said Umeo Koganemaru, chief advisor of the Japan International Cooperation Agency was there.

Ambassadors from Austria, Bolivia, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Cuba, Germany, Greece, Guatemala, Japan, Malaysia, Panama, Poland, Romania, South Korea, Spain, Venezuela and the European Community were being held according to various reports.
Panama named its ambassador Carlos Luis Linares and said he was among 18 ambassadors being held. Reports suggested the rest included:
Austria named its ambassador as Arthur Schuschnigg.
Bolivia named its ambassador as Jorge Gumucio.
Brazil named its ambassador as Carlos Luiz.
Bulgaria named its ambassador as Dimitar Stanoev.
Canada named its ambassador as Anthony Vincent.
Cuba named its ambassador as Pedro Diaz Arcia.
Germany named its ambassador as Heribert Woeckel and said two other German diplomats were being held.
Greece named its ambassador as Alkiviades Karokis.
Guatemala named its ambassador Jose Maria Argueta.
Japan named its ambassador as Morihisa Aoki and said 12 more Japanese embassy staff were being held.
Poland named its charge d'affaires as Wojciech Tomaszewski.
Romania named its charge d'affaires as Octavian Filip.
South Korea named its ambassador as Lee Won-young.
Spain named its charge d'affaires Estanislao de Grandes.
Venezuela named its ambassador as Horacio Artega.
It was not clear whether Malaysia or the European Community had confirmed their ambassadors were being held. The United States declined to say whether any Americans were among the hostages.
Britain said at least one member of embassy staff was there.
Japanese firms in Peru said the following staff were held:
Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. Ltd. -- Shigeru Taki, head of Matsushita Peru and three Japanese staff.
Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co. Ltd. -- Shuji Saito, head of energy department at Tokyo headquarters, Yoshiaki Kitagawa, head of Lima branch and four Japanese staff.
Tomen Corp. -- Atsushi Iwamoto, Lima branch head and one Peruvian staff.
Nissho Iwai Corp. -- Lima branch head Shigenori Sato and one Japanese staff
Kanematsu Corp. -- Lima branch head Atsushi Morizono and one Japanese staff
Mitsui & Co. Ltd -- Masami Kobayashi, head of Mitsui Peru and three Japanese staff.
Marubeni Corp.-- Keiichi Saito, head of Lima branch and two Japanese staff.
Mitsubishi Corp. -- Akira Miyashita, head of Mitsubishi Peru and two Japanese staff.
Ajinomoto Co. Inc. -- Yoshihiko Sakai, head of Ajinomoto Peru and two staff.
NEC Corp. -- Lima branch head Masazumi Takada and one Japanese staff.
Toyota Motor Corp. -- Masaru Tomita, head of Toyota Peru and one Japanese staff.
Nissan Motor Co. Ltd. -- Head of Nissan Peru Carlos Canbana.
Asahi Chemical Industry Co. Ltd. -- Hideo Nozaki, head of Asahi Chemical Peru.
Fujita Corp. -- Shunsuke Fujita, Lima branch head.
Japan Water Works (Jogesuido) Co. -- Nobuo Matsunaga, head of local project manager and four Japanese staff.
Japan Airlines (JAL) Co. Ltd. -- Masanori Sugimaru, head of local affiliate.
Japan Bonita and Tuna Fishing Association -- Tateo Kawakami, head of Lima branch.
Other hostages were believed to be members of Japanese associations and school staff:
Teachers sent to Japanese school in Lima -- Shigeru Yamazaki and four staff.
Members of 12 Japanese associations -- Ten Japanese and 22 Japanese-Peruvians.
